summary: Include 94/123 as well as 94/124 in the quotation reference
rationale: The first clause komaḥti maye ʕal u qaṭmawo is in 94/123. The second clause W bəṯr konəsli am mayanək is in 94/124. The existing reference covers only the second clause. The automatic alternative 94/240 concerns cooking meat dumplings and is not the source of this example.

data.turoyo: Ad dawġani, həngi d kətne zaḥf, komaḥtənne naqlawat b ak kise, konəṣli am maye mənne w kofayši ad dawġe, kowən xd u layšo, kəmmínanne ǧaǧəq.
data.translation: Wenn man sehr viel Ayran hat, tut man ihn manchmal in Beutel Dann tropft das Wasser von ihm ab und der Ayran bleibt. Er wird dann wie Teig, und wir nennen ihn dann dschādschiq.

rationale: Second Infectum example; complete dairy-draining process with explicit m- source, contrasting inherited ash-water dripping.

summary: Both occurrences checked. 94/124 is already the inherited example, so it is not repeated. 94/199 fills the thin Infectum cell without adding a new sense.
Plural am maye agrees with konəṣli. The m- phrase mənne names the source material, not an agent; the process has no overt causer.
Printed konəsli at 94/124 differs from the inherited ko-nəṣli. The source s is retained in analysis; no silent emphatic-consonant correction is proposed without source verification.
Is s in 94/124 konəsli a transcription convention, a printing error or an actual consonant variant? Compare with emphatic ṣ in 94/199.
Dripping water can drain from bagged ayran as well as ash; the different material source does not change tropfen.
